## Overview

`GXBioAge` (Gompertz-X Biological Age; the suffix "X" denotes five
clinical laboratory biomarkers used for model construction) estimates
biological age (BioAge) from a Gompertz survival regression. The model
was trained on NHANES data using chronological age and five routine
blood markers.

> **v0.3.0 note:** this release adds two ggplot2-based batch-result
> visualisations — `plot_bioage_cor()` (a density-coloured scatter
> of BioAge vs. chronological age with R / MAE / p-value annotation)
> and `plot_bioage_diff()` (a two-panel BioAgeDiff diagnostic).
> `predict_bioage_file()` now accepts a `plot_dir` argument that
> dumps both PNGs into the chosen directory.
>
> **v0.2.0 note:** the previous release dropped the *Uric Acid (UA)*
> marker that was used in v0.1.0; the model is now trained on five
> markers (TC, CRP, PLT, CREA, WBC).

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install("path/to/GXBioAge")
# The plotting functions need ggplot2 (+ MASS is recommended).
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "MASS"))
```

## Usage

### Single subject

```{r}
library(GXBioAge)
calc_bioage(age = 55, TC = 5.1, CRP = 1.5,
            PLT = 230, CREA = 0.85, WBC = 6.2)
```

### Batch on a data frame

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  ID   = c("S001", "S002", "S003"),
  Age  = c(55, 65, 32),
  TC   = c(5.1, 6.5, 4.2),
  CRP  = c(1.5, 8.0, 0.5),
  PLT  = c(230, 280, 220),
  CREA = c(0.85, 1.40, 0.75),
  WBC  = c(6.2, 9.5, 5.4)
)
predict_bioage(df)
```

### Read CSV / write results

```{r, eval = FALSE}
predict_bioage_file(
  system.file("extdata", "example_input.csv", package = "GXBioAge"),
  out = "results.csv"
)
```

### Batch visualisations

`plot_bioage_cor()` draws a density-coloured scatter of BioAge vs.
chronological age with a linear regression overlay and a labelled
annotation box reporting Pearson's R, the mean absolute error
(MAE) and the p-value:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)}
big <- data.frame(
  Age  = c(55, 65, 32, 50, 72, 45, 60, 38, 80, 28,
           58, 47, 68, 41, 75, 53, 36, 62, 49, 70),
  TC   = c(5.1, 6.5, 4.2, 5.2, 5.8, 4.8, 5.5, 4.5, 6.0, 4.0,
           5.4, 4.9, 5.7, 4.6, 5.9, 5.0, 4.3, 5.6, 5.0, 5.8),
  CRP  = c(1.5, 8.0, 0.5, 2.4, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.8, 4.0, 0.4,
           1.8, 1.2, 3.5, 0.6, 3.2, 1.6, 0.5, 2.6, 1.0, 3.8),
  PLT  = c(230, 280, 220, 240, 260, 235, 250, 225, 270, 215,
           245, 230, 275, 220, 265, 240, 220, 255, 235, 268),
  CREA = c(0.85, 1.40, 0.75, 0.90, 1.10, 0.80, 0.95, 0.78, 1.20, 0.72,
           0.92, 0.82, 1.15, 0.76, 1.18, 0.88, 0.74, 1.05, 0.83, 1.22),
  WBC  = c(6.2, 9.5, 5.4, 7.0, 7.8, 6.0, 6.8, 5.8, 8.2, 5.2,
           6.6, 6.0, 8.0, 5.6, 7.6, 6.4, 5.4, 7.2, 6.0, 8.4)
)
res <- predict_bioage(big, keep = TRUE)
plot_bioage_cor(res)
```

`plot_bioage_diff()` adds a one-page BioAgeDiff diagnostic
(histogram + Bland-Altman-style scatter) so the calibration of
the model against chronological age is easy to inspect:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
plot_bioage_diff(res)
```

Both plots can also be requested directly from
`predict_bioage_file()` via the `plot_dir` argument:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
predict_bioage_file(
  system.file("extdata", "example_input.csv", package = "GXBioAge"),
  out      = "results.csv",
  plot_dir = "plots"
)
```

## Model

For any individual,

```
BioAge = ( β_age · Age + Σ βᵢ · Xᵢ + log(γ₂/γ₁) ) / β_age
```

where β_age comes from an age-only Gompertz model, βᵢ are marker
coefficients from a model on Age + markers, and the age coefficient
in the marker model is constrained to equal β_age. The term
log(γ₂/γ₁) absorbs the difference in baseline rates between the
two models.

A positive `BioAgeDiff` indicates that the blood-marker profile
carries excess mortality risk relative to peers of the same
chronological age — i.e. *accelerated biological aging*.

## Units

Input units must match the training units:

| Variable | Unit |
|---|---|
| Age  | years |
| TC   | mmol/L |
| CRP  | mg/L |
| PLT  | 10⁹/L |
| CREA | mg/dL |
| WBC  | 10⁹/L |
